programs.title_tr: Pratt & Whitney GTF (PW1100G) Toz Metal Kusuru & Yere İndirmeler
programs.title_en: Pratt & Whitney GTF (PW1100G) Powder Metal Defect & Groundings
programs.current_status_tr: Yüksek basınçlı türbin disklerindeki mikroskobik toz metal kirliliği nedeniyle küresel çapta yüzlerce A320neo/A321neo uçağı planlanmamış motor bakımına alındı. Ortalama motor revizyon süresi (TAT) 250-300 günü buluyor.
programs.current_status_en: Contaminated powder metal in high-pressure turbine disks required accelerated inspections; hundreds of A320neo family jets grounded globally with MRO shop turnaround times reaching 250-300 days.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: THY filosundaki yaklaşık 30-40 adet A320/A321neo uçağı yerde bekliyor; kapasite açığını kapatmak için ıslak kiralama (wet lease) ve mevcut A320ceo uçaklarının hizmet ömrünü uzatma yoluna gidildi. Pegasus filosu ağırlıklı CFM LEAP motorlu olduğu için doğrudan etkilenmedi.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: Turkish Airlines has 30-40 A321neo aircraft parked; capacity shortfall managed via wet leases and extending older A320ceo service lives. Pegasus remains largely unaffected due to CFM LEAP engine selection.
programs.timeline_horizon: 2026 yılı boyunca ve 2027 ilk yarısına kadar sürmesi bekleniyor.
programs.source_reference: RTX Corporation / FAA Airworthiness Directives (AD 2024-0044) / THY KAP Açıklamaları

programs.title_tr: Boeing 737 MAX Üretim Kısıtı (FAA Aylık 38 Tavanı) & Tedarik Zinciri
programs.title_en: Boeing 737 MAX FAA Monthly 38 Cap & Supply Chain Bottlecks
programs.current_status_tr: FAA'in kalite ve montaj denetimleri kapsamında Boeing 737 üretimini aylık 38 uçak tavanında tutması ve Spirit AeroSystems gövde teslimat gecikmeleri nedeniyle 2026 teslimat takvimleri 3-6 ay geriye ötelendi. MAX 7 ve MAX 10 sertifikasyonu gecikmeye devam ediyor.
programs.current_status_en: FAA capped 737 production at 38/month pending quality audit milestones; Spirit AeroSystems fuselage supply constraints pushed airline delivery slots back by 3 to 6 months. MAX 7 and MAX 10 certification remains pending.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: SunExpress ve THY teslimatları planlanan takvimin gerisinde seyrediyor; havayolları yoğun yaz ve sonbahar kapasite planlamalarını mevcut gövdelerle optimize ediyor.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: SunExpress and Turkish Airlines delivery streams experiencing slot postponements; carriers optimizing utilization on existing fleet assets.
programs.timeline_horizon: Aylık 38 üretim tavanının 2026 sonuna kadar aşamalı olarak artırılması hedefleniyor.
programs.source_reference: FAA Oversight Directives / Boeing Quarterly Deliveries / Airline Fleet Filings

programs.title_tr: Airbus A321XLR Ticari Teslimatları & Dar Gövde Uzun Menzil Devrimi
programs.title_en: Airbus A321XLR Entry into Service & Long-Range Narrowbody Wave
programs.current_status_tr: EASA tip sertifikasyonunu tamamlayan A321XLR, Iberia tarafından Madrid-Boston hattında ilk ticari uçuşlarına başladı. 4.700 deniz mili (8.700 km) menziliyle dar gövdede transatlantik ve kıtalararası uçuş maliyetlerini %30 düşürüyor.
programs.current_status_en: Having achieved EASA certification, the A321XLR commenced transatlantic operations with launch customer Iberia. Its 4,700 nm range unlocks thin long-haul routes at 30% lower trip cost.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: Orta Doğu, Afrika ve ikincil Avrupa şehirlerine doğrudan bağlantı potansiyeli nedeniyle bölge taşıyıcıları tarafından yakından izleniyor. THY ve Pegasus filo stratejilerinde uzun vadeli alternatif.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: Closely monitored by regional carriers for secondary point-to-point routes into Africa, Central Asia and Europe; potential long-term fit for Istanbul network.
programs.source_reference: EASA Type Certificate Data Sheet (TCDS) / Airbus Commercial Aircraft Updates

programs.title_tr: Boeing 777-9 (777X) Test Uçuşları & Hizmete Giriş Tarihi
programs.current_status_tr: İtiş kolu bağlantı elemanındaki (thrust link) teknik arıza sonrası test uçuşları geçici olarak durdurulmuştu; Boeing ilk teslimat takvimini 2026 yılına (ve potansiyel olarak 2027'ye) revize etti. Başta Emirates ve Lufthansa olmak üzere amiral gemisi filoları A380 ve 777-300ER ömür uzatmak zorunda kaldı.
programs.current_status_en: Structural component inspection on engine thrust links required test fleet pause; initial deliveries rescheduled to 2026/2027. Major customers Emirates and Lufthansa forced to extend legacy 777-300ER and A380 service lives.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: THY'nin geniş gövde siparişlerinde Airbus A350-1000'e ağırlık vermesinde 777X gecikmeleri belirleyici stratejik etken oldu.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: Delays were a primary catalyst for Turkish Airlines' decision to anchor its high-capacity widebody order book on the Airbus A350-1000.
programs.timeline_horizon: FAA tip sertifikasyonu ve ilk ticari teslimat 2026 sonu / 2027 hedefleniyor.
programs.source_reference: Boeing Defense, Space & Security / Airline IR Filings / Emirates President Statements

programs.title_tr: CFM LEAP-1A / 1B Yüksek Basınç Türbini Dayanıklılığı & MRO Bekleme Süreleri
programs.title_en: CFM LEAP-1A / 1B Hot-Section Durability & Shop Visit Backlogs
programs.current_status_tr: Sıcak iklim, tozlu hava sahası ve yüksek iniş-kalkış döngüsü altında çalışan LEAP motorlarında türbin kanatçığı erozyonu nedeniyle planlanandan erken motor indirme yaşanıyor. Küresel MRO atölyelerinde yedek parça ve motor kıtlığı devam ediyor.
programs.current_status_en: Harsh environment operations (heat, sand, high cycle utilization) causing premature hot-section turbine blade wear; global MRO shops experiencing parts constraints and extended turn-around times.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: Pegasus'un filosunun belkemiğini oluşturan A321neo uçaklarında CFM LEAP-1A motorları kullanılıyor. Pegasus, proaktif motor rotasyonu ve yedek motor rezervasyonu ile uçak yerde kalma süresini (AOG) asgaride tutuyor.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: Pegasus relies heavily on CFM LEAP-1A on its A321neo fleet; carrier leverages proactive engine rotation and buffer lease pools to keep AOG rates minimal.
programs.timeline_horizon: CFM'in güncellenmiş dayanıklı parça (durability kit) teslimatları 2026 boyunca yaygınlaşıyor.
programs.source_reference: Safran / GE Aerospace Engine Technical Briefings / Aviation Week MRO Watch

DUBAI, UAE, 05 November 2026: The Emirates Group today announced its half-year financial results, posting a profit before tax of AED 4.1 billion (US$ 1.1 billion) for the first six months of 2026-27, a remarkable performance against the disruption and high fuel prices caused by the ongoing conflict in the Gulf region. After accounting for income tax charges, the Group’s profit after tax is AED 3.6 billion (US$ 1.0 billion), down 66% from last year. Illustrating its strong operating performance, the Group achieved an EBITDA of AED 12.5 billion (US$ 3.4 billion), 41% lower than the AED 21.1 billion (US$ 5.7 billion) reported for the same period last year where the Group had set a new record for profit and revenue. Group revenue was AED 66.2 billion (US$ 18.0 billion) for the first six months of 2026-27, down 12% from AED 75.4 billion (US$ 20.6 billion) last year. The Group closed the first half year of 2026-27 with a cash position of AED 54.1 billion (US$ 14.7 billion) on 30 September 2026, compared to AED 59.6 billion (US$ 16.2 billion) on 31 March 2026. The Group has been able to tap on its own strong cash reserves to support business needs, including pre-delivery payments for aircraft and servicing existing debt obligations. The Group also paid the remaining AED 2 billion (US$ 545 million) in dividend to its owner, the Investment Corporation of Dubai (ICD), of the AED 3.5 billion (US$ 953 million) declared for the financial year 2025-26. His Highness (HH) Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed Al Maktoum, Chairman and Chief Executive, Emirates Airline and Group said: “It has been a demanding six months, and once again our business model and our people stood up to the test. Against unprecedented regional challenges and high fuel prices, the Group has delivered a profit before tax of AED 4.1 billion (US$ 1.1 billion). Customer demand held firm and our cargo operations made a strong contribution, keeping revenue and cash levels healthy even as global jet fuel prices doubled against the same period last year, impacting our costs and profitability. “I’d like to thank the UAE government for its decisive response and its co-ordination of all stakeholders to enable the safe resumption of air transport in the aftermath of military activity across the Gulf region. The government’s measures have also led to the easing of travel advisories to and through the UAE. This has allowed us to restore our operations with confidence and to keep serving our customers and communities. “Throughout this time, we have not paused our investments. Emirates and dnata continue to commit significant resources to expand our fleet, enhance our products and services, and develop capabilities that will shape the future of our business. This is how we stay ahead and stay resilient to external challenges.” HH Sheikh Ahmed added: “We enter the second half of our 2026-27 financial year with measured optimism. While keeping a close watch on costs and geopolitical developments, we remain focused on delivering what Emirates and dnata are known for – safety, quality, and customer satisfaction. We’ve weathered challenges before, and with our strong cash position and solid foundation built up over the years, the Group is well-placed to navigate the headwinds of volatility and high fuel prices.” Compared to 31 March 2026, the Emirates Group’s employee base dropped by 2% to an overall count of 128,237 on 30 September 2026. However, both Emirates and dnata maintain ongoing recruitment drives to support business requirements. Emirates airline The first six months of 2026-27 brought significant challenges to Emirates’ operations as intermittent airspace restrictions and closures across the region tested the airline’s operational agility, while government travel advisories reshaped consumer choices and travel flows. During this period, Emirates focused on restoring its network and connectivity options through its Dubai hub. At 30 September, Emirates was operating 91% of its pre-disruption network, with its passenger and cargo network spanning 150 airports in 78 countries and territories. The airline also launched a series of initiatives to boost customer confidence, including an industry-first comprehensive travel cover that is unrestricted by government travel advisories, free date changes on booked tickets, and generous refund policies. Between 1 April and 30 September, Emirates expanded its inventory of Premium Economy seats and brought its latest cabin products to customers in even more markets, as it received delivery of 9 new A350 aircraft and completed the full cabin refurbishment of 12 aircraft (9 A380s, 3 Boeing 777s). Emirates’ retrofit programme , one of the world’s largest known such projects, represents a planned investment of over US$ 7.0 billion to bring Emirates’ latest cabin products across its fleet. The airline’s Starlink installation programme also continued at pace, equipping 36 more aircraft with high-speed Wi-Fi in the sky during the first six months of the year, and bringing Emirates’ total Starlink-installed fleet to 57 aircraft as of 30 September. To support its future fleet requirements, in May, Emirates broke ground on its US$ 5.1 billion engineering and Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul (MRO) facility at Al Maktoum International Airport, with completion expected in the mid-2030s. Leading from the front even in testing times, Emirates launched two industry-first cabin products to rave customer reviews: the U-dream headrest built into Economy Class seats, and electronically controlled privacy dividers in Premium Economy . These innovations have raised the bar for Economy and Premium Economy travel, redefining comfort and privacy for customers in these cabin classes. On the ground, Emirates inaugurated the first of its new concept lounges in Munich, Frankfurt and Manchester, featuring the airline’s latest interior design palette and elevated services for premium customers and frequent flyers. Emirates also opened new travel stores bringing its total retail footprint over 30 stores, offering customers more personal and experiential service touchpoints. Emirates continued its efforts to make travel more inclusive with the roll-out of Travel Rehearsals at 15 more stations across the UK, Australia, Portugal, the Philippines, Madagascar and the Maldives in the first half of 2026-27. This successful programme, which has now run in 47 stations, supports young travellers with autism and their families, helping them build confidence and reduce travel anxiety via exposure to real-time airport and flight simulations. The airline also continued to make a positive impact on communities , working with partners to deliver CSR programmes across key markets. In the first half of the year, initiatives included: the opening of a renovated community tennis court in Miami as part of the Force for Good programme with the USTA Foundation; a refreshed youth technology and gaming room in New York City with NBA Cares; a new natural play area with the London Wildlife Trust as part of the Championing Nature programme with Wimbledon; and the launch of the Emirates Nourishment Programme to deliver 400,000 breakfasts annually to underprivileged kids across South Africa in partnership with EPCR and the Kolisi Foundation. During the first half of 2026-27, Emirates extended its successful and long-running sponsorship deals with Arsenal Football Club (until 2033), and with Real Madrid (until 2031), representing multi-year investments in global brand visibility and partnerships with two of the world’s most prominent clubs in football. Overall capacity during the first six months of the year decreased by 10% to 28.2 billion Available Tonne Kilometres (ATKM) due to a reduced flying schedule. Capacity measured in Available Seat Kilometres (ASKM), decreased by 17%, whilst passenger traffic carried measured in Revenue Passenger Kilometres (RPKM) was down by 25% with an average Passenger Seat Factor of 72.0%, compared with 79.5% during the same period last year. Emirates carried 21.8 million passengers between 1 April and 30 September 2026, down 22% from the same period last year. Emirates SkyCargo transported 1.2 million tonnes in the first six months of the year, down by 1% compared to the same period last year. However, cargo revenue increased by 52% as the regional conflict reduced available airfreight capacity while concurrently pushing shippers to seek airfreight options due to marine transport disruptions. In the first half of 2026-27, Emirates SkyCargo added capacity from 5 new Boeing 777 freighters delivered, and the deployment of its first passenger-to-freighter converted aircraft. The cargo division expanded its freighter network with two new destinations, Almaty and Zhengzhou; introduced dedicated freighter services to over 15 existing Emirates destinations; and increased frequencies to several key markets including in the Far East. Emirates profit before tax for the first half of 2026-27 reached AED 3.7 billion (US$ 1.0 billion), compared to its record performance of AED 11.4 billion (US$ 3.1 billion) for the same period last year. Emirates profit after tax is AED 3.3 billion (US$ 903 million), down 66%. Emirates revenue , including other operating income, of AED 56.9 billion (US$ 15.5 billion) was down 13% compared with AED 65.6 billion (US$ 17.9 billion) last year. The airline’s revenue performance can be attributed to enduring travel demand across its markets, particularly for Emirates’ premium cabins, and a solid contribution from the airline’s cargo business. Emirates’ operating costs (including fuel) dropped by 2% in line with operations. Despite a 12% reduction in fuel uplift due to lower operations, Emirates’ fuel costs, before hedging gains, rose by 60% compared with the previous half-year. Gains of AED 7.1 billion from its fuel price risk management strategy significantly offset the impact of higher fuel prices, reducing the net fuel cost increase to 13%. Fuel remains the largest component of the airline’s operating cost at 34%. Emirates’ EBITDA of AED 11.5 billion (US$ 3.1 billion) remained healthy, down 41% compared to AED 19.7 billion (US$ 5.4 billion) for the same period last year. Emirates Flight Catering revenue from external customers declined by 51% to AED 273 million (US$ 74 million). Its uplift of 4.5 million airline meals was down by 41% due to reduced air traffic at Dubai’s airport during the period. Emirates Leisure Retail/MMI revenue declined by 13% to AED 1.2 billion, due to the impact of lower tourism traffic in the UAE during the first six months of 2026-27. dnata dnata’s airport operations, catering and retail, and travel services divisions adapted quickly to business and operating challenges caused by the regional conflict, with its international businesses helping to offset the impact of reduced airline and travel traffic in the UAE and the broader Gulf region. In the first half of 2026-27, dnata continued to win customers with its safe and high-quality services across its global operations, signing multi-year agreements, including a cargo partnership with Silk Way Group in Singapore and inflight catering contracts with Cathay Pacific across several airports in the UK and the USA. Notably, dnata Airport Operations secured a seven-year ground handling license at Amsterdam Schiphol Airport, reinforcing its position at one of Europe’s key aviation hubs. dnata continued to make strategic investments to grow its capabilities and enhance its customer offering. In the first six months this year, dnata opened a new integrated command centre to support its growing cargo operations in Dubai; committed to an AED 8 million investment to expand The Fort – Lisaili, Arabian Adventures’ desert tourism destination in Dubai; and continued to invest in advanced technology and equipment across its operations including automated aircraft approach systems in Dubai, an aircraft catering simulator in Dublin, and autonomous tractor trials in Europe and Asia. In addition, dnata announced an AU$ 32 million investment to build a new cargo facility at Western Sydney International Airport (WSI), while construction of its new catering facility at WSI is on track for a 2027 opening. It also continued to deliver its global cargo and logistics strategy through targeted investments across its network, commissioning its new AED 100 million (US$ 27 million) logistics facility in Dubai South and progressing strategic developments, including a planned AED 37 million investment in Alat, Azerbaijan, alongside new and expanded cargo operations at East Midlands Airport and Zurich Airport. In its Travel division, dnata integrated its Imagine Cruising and Travelbag businesses, bringing together two complementary portfolios to build greater scale, share expertise, and drive international growth. dnata’s revenue , including other operating income, reached AED 11.0 billion (US$ 3.0 billion) down by 7% compared to AED 11.7 billion (US$ 3.2 billion) generated in the same period last year. Overall profit before tax for dnata was AED 410 million (US$ 112 million), down by 51% from the same period last year. dnata’s profit after tax is AED 309 million (US$ 84 million), down 56% from last year. Illustrating its operating performance, dnata’s EBITDA was AED 939 million (US$ 256 million), down 31% from last year’s AED 1.4 billion (US$ 372 million). dnata’s airport operations remain the largest contributor to revenue with AED 5.4 billion (US$ 1.5 billion), a 3% decrease compared to the same period last year, as its growing global business offset the reduction of customer airline operations at its UAE hub during this period. Across dnata’s operations, the number of aircraft turns handled decreased by 8% to 414,012, and it recorded 1.49 million tonnes of cargo handled , down by 6%. dnata’s flight catering and retail operations contributed AED 4.2 billion (US$ 1.1 billion) to its revenue, up 1%, driven by its growing inflight retail business notably with EasyJet and Aer Lingus. The overall number of meals uplifted was 54.0 million, down 10% compared to last year, largely due to the loss of key contracts in its UK operations. dnata's travel division contributed AED 1.4 billion (US$ 373 million) to revenue, down 31% compared to AED 2.0 billion (US$ 538 million) for the same period last year, primarily due to its divestment of Travel Republic and Netflights in the UK, which ceased new bookings from November 2025. The travel division reported an underlying total transactional value (TTV) of AED 3.8 billion (US$ 1.0 billion), down 22% compared to AED 5.0 billion (US$ 1.4 billion) for the same period last year.

stories.headline: European Aviation Network Traffic Drops 2.3% Week-on-Week Amid Weather Disruptions
stories.lead: European flight volumes fell to an average of 32,480 daily flights due to adverse weather and reduced capacity across major operators. Despite the weekly dip, overall network traffic remained 0.7% higher than the corresponding week in 2025.
stories.source_description: The network averaged 32,480 daily flights (including overflights), down 2.3% from Week 42 and 0.7% higher compared to the same week in 2025. Storms Austen and Boelo caused widespread flight disruptions across northern and western Europe between 23-25 October 2026. Among the 10 busiest carriers, capacity declined by an average of 1.3% week-on-week. Pegasus was the only carrier to record growth (+1%), while the KLM Group registered the largest decrease (-4%). Flight volumes across the 10 busiest States fell by an average of 2.5% with none recording growth. Greece saw the most significant decrease (-7%). Network arrival and departure punctuality were 73.5% and 69.4%, better than in the equivalent week of 2025. En-route ATFM delays decreased by 12% compared to the previous week, with a daily average of circa 54K delay minutes, and were 6% above 2025 levels. Total air traffic flow management (ATFM) delay was 2.4 min/flight (1.7 for en-route and 0.7 for airport). ATC capacity & staffing was the top delay cause (65% of all en-route ATFM delays), followed by weather (20%).

stories.headline: Boeing Commercial Market Outlook Projects Global Fleet Growth to 2045
stories.lead: Boeing forecasts that the global commercial aircraft fleet will grow nearly 80% to over 50,000 airplanes by 2045. Airlines and cargo operators will require nearly 44,000 new aircraft over the next 20 years to support air travel and cargo expansion.
stories.source_description: The global commercial airplanes fleet is expected to grow nearly 80% to more than 50,000 airplanes by 2045 as airlines and cargo operators add capacity. Globally, operators are forecasted to need nearly 44,000 new airplanes to support sustained air travel demand and air cargo expansion over the next 20 years. The global single-aisle fleet will nearly double to more than 36,000 jets, serving core short-haul networks and operating more than half of all global capacity. More than 8,000 widebody airplanes will be in service in 2045, enabling long-haul passenger routes, enhanced passenger experience and critical air cargo capacity. Air cargo traffic growth and the need for new-technology freighters to renew the fleet will drive demand for more than 2,900 production and converted freighters. Passenger traffic is expected to grow 4% annually, resulting in a doubling of global air traffic between 2026 and 2045.

stories.headline: Emirates Launches Nourishment Programme for South African Youth
stories.lead: Emirates, in partnership with EPCR and the Kolisi Foundation, has initiated a long-term programme to support children in South Africa through nutrition and education.
stories.source_description: More than 800 Cape Town primary school students took part in a day of nutrition, rugby, education and creativity as part of the Emirates Nourishment Programme Emirates, EPCR and the Kolisi Foundation were joined by DHL Stormers players including Siya Kolisi to inspire children through rugby, teamwork and positive role models The long-term programme aims to support 2,000 children every year across Cape Town, Johannesburg and Durban, helping them overcome barriers to learning and reach their potential Cape Town, South Africa, 4 November 2026 – More than 800 primary school students in Cape Town enjoyed a day of rugby, learning and creativity as Emirates, European Professional Club Rugby (EPCR) and the Kolisi Foundation brought the Emirates Nourishment Programme to life at a local school. Joined by DHL Stormers players, Kolisi Foundation founder Siya Kolisi, Emirates Cabin Crew and team members from South Africa and Dubai, and EPCR representatives, the partners showed how good nutrition, education and the power of sport can help children build confidence and realise their potential. The day began with the Emirates Nourishment Programme, as the partners helped prepare and serve breakfast porridge, ensuring the school’s children started their day nourished and ready to learn. A nutritious breakfast can make a meaningful difference to a child’s ability to concentrate, participate in class and make the most of learning opportunities. The activation offered a glimpse into the wider work of the Emirates Nourishment Programme, a multi-year initiative delivered by the Kolisi Foundation in partnership with Emirates and EPCR. The programme aims to provide approximately 400,000 nutritious breakfasts annually, reaching around 2,000 learners each year through participating schools and Early Childhood Development centres. By helping children access breakfast consistently, the programme seeks to support their readiness to learn and participate in school. Afzal Parambil, Emirates’ Regional Manager of Southern Africa said, “At Emirates, we believe meaningful partnerships are those that make a lasting difference. Through the Emirates Nourishment Programme, we’re working with our partners to support children in ways that go beyond the classroom – providing nutrition to help them learn, access to resources that support their education and connecting them with inspiring role models. It’s a privilege to be part of an initiative that invests in South Africa’s next generation and reflects Emirates’ longstanding commitment to supporting the communities we serve.” Mahlatse Mashua, Managing Director of the Kolisi Foundation , said, “Meaningful impact starts with understanding the barriers children face and being intentional about addressing them. What makes this partnership special is how it brings nutrition, education and sport together in a sustained approach. Ultimately, the measure of a successful partnership is not simply what we do together, but what becomes possible for the children we serve.” Following breakfast, DHL Stormers players took to the school grounds to lead an engaging rugby clinic. Through fun drills and small-sided games, Siya Kolisi, Lukhanyo Vokozela, BJ Dixon, Markus Muller, Ruan Ackermann, Leolin Zas, Vernon Matongo and JJ Kotze introduced students to the fundamentals of the game, while encouraging teamwork, communication, resilience and problem-solving – skills that extend well beyond the rugby field. Siya Kolisi, Founder of the Kolisi Foundation , said, “Every child is born with potential, but not every child has the same opportunity to realise it. Whether it’s access to nutritious food, learning resources or someone who believes in them, our responsibility is to help remove those barriers. Today is incredibly special, but what excites me most is that this programme goes beyond today. It’s about giving every child the opportunity to thrive.” With the DHL Stormers also joining the activities, the day gave students the opportunity to learn from sporting role models who demonstrate what can be achieved through perseverance, collaboration and belief in oneself. DHL Stormers’ Vernon Matongo who participated in the activity, said, “It was special to see what Emirates, EPCR and the Kolisi Foundation are doing. Some of those kids will only have the meal from the Nourishment Programme that they get in the morning, and that's it for the day. And then they must concentrate in class, play sport in the afternoon. I don't think any kid should have to go through those circumstances. “In a team, you get to know your teammates stories, and some players in the Stormers came from similar backgrounds. So, I think it's very important to go and give back. Being able to contribute is massive, being able to see that was special for us. The kids from the programme also came to the game (against Bristol Bears) and it was very special to have them there.” Further supporting early education, Emirates delivered 820 backpacks from the Aircrafted KIDS collection to the primary school, each equipped with stationery, water bottles and age-appropriate books written by local authors. Blending culturally rich stories with interactive learning opportunities, the books encourage children to explore new ideas, develop a love of reading and swap stories with their classmates. Aircrafted KIDS supports early childhood education by providing essential school supplies and helping remove a common barrier to learning: access to resources. To date, nearly 4,000 Aircrafted KIDS backpacks have been distributed to schools and community centres around the globe. The students also put their creativity to work in a bag charm workshop, making personalised decorations for their Aircrafted KIDS backpacks, using upcycled leather repurposed from Emirates’ A380 and Boeing 777 aircraft. Led by Maite Gonzalez Eizaguirre, Head of Emirates Aircrafted at Emirates Engineering and assisted by Emirates Cabin Crew and team members, the session introduced students to the possibilities of upcycling, showing how materials can be given a new purpose through imagination and craftsmanship. Brenda Mangali, the school principal said, “They say it takes a village to raise a child, and today is a beautiful reminder of that. We are incredibly grateful to have partners, parents and our community come together around our children. Beyond the excitement of today, the greatest gift is the message it sends to every learner: you matter, you are valued, and we believe in your future.” Jacques Raynaud, EPCR CEO , said, “This programme shows what rugby can do beyond the pitch. Seeing the DHL Stormers players, our partners and the children share breakfast, a training session and a creative afternoon together is exactly what we hoped this programme would bring. Through impACT, our CSR strategy, we want our competitions to leave a positive and lasting legacy in the communities that welcome them, and South Africa is now very much part of our rugby family. We are proud to stand alongside Emirates and the Kolisi Foundation to help these children start every school day ready to learn.” The school’s exterior was also given a colourful new addition, through a collaborative mural created with Cape Town-based artist Skhumbuzo Salman , the founder and creative force behind Skubalisto art . Painted on one of the school walls, the mural celebrates South Africa’s natural beauty, featuring Table Mountain, protea flowers and lush foliage. At its centre, a young person stands against the vibrant landscape, highlighting the importance of water as the foundation of life and the need to protect this resource. The learners played an integral role in bringing the artwork to life, painting most of the mural’s vibrant background. For many, it was their first time working with spray paint, yet they approached the challenge with confidence and enthusiasm, making a significant contribution to the finished artwork. The process transformed the mural into a shared creative achievement, giving the children an opportunity to develop new skills, express themselves and take pride in a lasting piece of art within their school community, while reinforcing the importance of water conservation through hands-on participation. Skumbuzo Salman, founder of Skubalisto said, “Painting has a unique ability to communicate what words sometimes cannot. I wanted the children to be part of creating something meaningful for their school, something they could take pride in and recognise as their own. During the painting process, they started comparing the girl in the mural to their classmates and even debating what to name her. That was a powerful moment because it showed me that they were connecting with the artwork and making it part of their own story. The mural will remain at the school for years to come as a reminder of this day and the possibilities it represents. When children meet inspiring people and experience new things, they begin to imagine futures beyond what they already know. Whether one of them becomes a rugby player, a pilot, a member of cabin crew or follows an entirely different path, I hope the experience leaves them with a greater sense of what is possible.” Launched in June 2026, the Emirates Nourishment Programme brings together nutritional support and the inspirational power of rugby to help children overcome barriers to learning and development. Through schools and Early Childhood Development centres in Cape Town, Johannesburg and Durban, the programme aims to support 2,000 children each year with consistent access to breakfast, alongside opportunities to engage with inspirational role models. Since its launch in School Term 3, the programme has delivered more than 35,000 breakfasts across participating sites, between June and September 2026. Running until at least 2030, the programme represents a long-term investment in South Africa's children and their futures. By bringing together nutrition, education, sport and community engagement, Emirates, EPCR and the Kolisi Foundation are working to create an environment in which children can arrive at school ready to learn, discover their strengths and build the foundations for a brighter future.

stories.headline: Emirates Celebrates Diwali with Special Menus Across Nine Indian Destinations
stories.lead: Emirates is celebrating the Diwali festival by offering traditional Indian sweets and festive dining experiences for passengers traveling between Dubai and nine Indian cities on 7 and 8 November 2026.
stories.source_description: Dubai, UAE, 4 November 2026: Emirates is bringing the sparkle and spirit of Diwali to the skies, celebrating the Hindu festival of lights with traditional Indian delicacies, festive dining experiences and a world of entertainment. On 7 and 8 November, customers travelling between Dubai and nine Indian destinations - Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Kochi, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Thiruvananthapuram, Kolkata and Mumbai, can enjoy special Diwali sweets across all cabin classes while select Emirates lounges will serve an array of Indian favourites to mark the occasion. Traditional Diwali sweets served across all cabin classes Emirates customers travelling to and from India can enjoy a taste of Diwali with traditional Indian sweets served onboard. Premium Economy and Economy Class customers will be treated to motichoor laddu alongside their hot meal - delicate, golden chickpea flour pearls soaked in sugar syrup, infused with fragrant cardamom and saffron, and finished with pistachios. First and Business Class customers can also indulge in kaju pista roll , a rich, rose-flavoured confection made with cashews, pistachios, dried fruits and nuts, elegantly wrapped in edible silver leaf. Festive Indian cuisine and Diwali desserts in Emirates’ First and Business Class Lounges From 3 to 8 November, Emirates’ First and Business Class Lounges in Dubai will celebrate Diwali with a vibrant selection of Indian specialities. Customers can savour vada pav accompanied by tangy tamarind and refreshing mint chutneys, followed by an assortment of traditional desserts including malai sandwich , mango delight , malai roll and the much-loved gajar ka halwa . First Class customers can also raise a toast to the festivities with a specially crafted Spicy Saffron Martini or a refreshing Iced Masala Cooler mocktail. In Emirates’ Business Class Lounges in Dubai, the festive menu will feature savoury favourites including vegetable keema samosa , onion kachori and paneer potli samosa , served with tamarind and mint chutneys. For a sweet finish, customers can enjoy balushahi , mango rajbhog and mini kesari rasgullas . The celebrations will extend to Emirates’ lounges in Cape Town and Johannesburg, where customers can enjoy an assortment of traditional sweets including coconut ice , barfi and jalebi . Bollywood blockbusters, Indian TV and music on ice The Diwali celebrations continue onboard with a rich selection of Indian entertainment on Emirates’ award-winning inflight entertainment system, ice . Customers can choose from up to 157 Indian movies, including Bollywood titles such as Mardaani 3 , Mayasabha – The Hall of Illusion and Coolie , alongside a wide range of regional films in nine languages – Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Kannada, Marathi, Punjabi, Bhojpuri, Bengali and Gujarati. For those who prefer the small screen, ice offers 14 Indian TV programmes, including Pritam and Pedro , Looteri Dulhan and Crime Patrol - 26 Jurm, 26 Cases. Music lovers can also set the mood for the festivities with a selection of 40 Indian albums and playlists, bringing the sounds of Diwali to the skies. Read more
